messages:
tara: Quick thread: ran a KV-block fragmentation bakeoff comparing FP8 vs INT8 for KV-only quant on a new 13B bring-up. TL;DR: FP8 cuts KV memory ~25-30% but shows worse cold-start p95 when fragmentation > ~64KB. Small quality deltas on long-context evals. Details below.

chen: Nice — can you paste the exact run flags and model config?

tara: Repro snippet: 
```
# FP8
./run_bench --model llama-13b --kv-quant fp8 --kv-block 256 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --warm 200 --iters 1000
# INT8
./run_bench --model llama-13b --kv-quant int8 --kv-block 256 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --warm 200 --iters 1000
```

omar: Paste the raw numbers (mem + latencies + any eval deltas).

tara: Raw microbench (median of 5 runs):
```
FP8-KV block=256
KV mem: 3.1 GB
Total GPU mem: 10.2 GB
p50 latency: 28 ms
p95 latency: 82 ms
Coldstart p95: 210 ms

INT8-KV block=256
KV mem: 4.4 GB
Total GPU mem: 11.6 GB
p50: 25 ms
p95: 75 ms
Coldstart p95: 160 ms
```

nisha: Huh — FP8 is smaller but slower on tail. suspect extra dequant or misaligned kernels + extra memcpy on fragmented slabs. Did you capture kernel timelines?

tara: Yes captured traces (nvtx + trace). Fragmentation metric: average free bytes per slab after prefix cache snapshot. When avg_free > 64KB we see more p95 noise.

chen: How do you compute fragmentation exactly?

tara: We count partially filled KV slabs in the allocator and sum free bytes per slab, then divide by slab count => avg_free. Also log number_of_partial_slabs. Example from run: avg_free=82KB, partial_slabs=48.

kayla: What about accuracy / quality? any regen or hallucination diffs?

tara: Eval on our 1k long-context chat set: FP8 KV vs INT8 KV: exact-match -0.5% (FP8 worse), rouge +0.1%, perplexity +0.3%. Hallucination (heuristic) up ~1.2% on >2k token contexts. Not huge but visible on long contexts where KV errors accumulate.

benchmark-bot: Stored artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/1848001234/ (bench.json, traces.tgz) :thumbsup:

omar: Any config that makes FP8 competitive on tail?

tara: Yes — lowering KV block size helps. With block=64: FP8 KV mem 3.4GB, p50 26ms, p95 68ms, coldstart p95 140ms. So tradeoff: smaller blocks reduce fragmentation but slightly increase overall overhead. Also enabling a lightweight compaction job that runs during low load fixes most cases.

chen: So operational recommendation?

tara: For Dedicated/private pools with stable long-running prefixes -> FP8 is attractive (lower GPU memory => higher packing). For Hosted noisy workloads with many short-lived prefixes -> prefer INT8 or enable periodic compaction/fallback to INT8 on high-fragmentation hosts. We'll add an automatic fallback rule in routing: if avg_free>80KB and cold_p95 > threshold -> route to INT8 variant.

kayla: Can you open a ticket to add compaction + routing rule? also attach the reproduce script to the bench page.

tara: Filed RH-5128 for runtime compaction + RH-5129 for routing fallback. Repro script is in s3/1848001234/repro.sh.

omar: Great, can we schedule a short follow-up to decide rollout plan? 15m sync?

tara: Yup, scheduling 15m tomorrow. Thanks folks :raised_hands:
